sections.h2: What the Clerk and Recorder does in a house sale
sections.html:
When a house is sold, the El Paso County Clerk and Recorder files the deed that moves it from seller to buyer, along with the deed of trust and the release that go with a mortgage. The office also collects the state documentary fee at the moment the deed is filed.

Filing is what puts the sale in the public record, and until a deed is recorded the county records still show the old owner. Most sellers never visit, because the title or settlement company handles the filing after closing. Still, it helps to know what the office charges and why a filing can bounce back. Questions go to the recording department at (719) 520-6200 or recweb@elpasoco.com.

Since July 1, 2025, El Paso County charges a flat $43 to record a standard document, whatever the page count. On a deed that transfers title for more than $500, the state documentary fee is added at one cent for every $100 of the price.

The $43 breaks down as a $40 state-set flat fee, a $1 Electronic Recording Technology Board surcharge and a $2 electronic filing surcharge. The change follows House Bill 24-1269.

Document or serviceFee
Standard, oversized, plat or condo document$43 flat, any page count
Documentary fee on a deed (C.R.S. 39-13-102)$0.01 per $100 of consideration, when consideration is above $500
Land survey$43 per document plus a $10 County Surveyor fee
Copies of recorded documents$0.25 per page, certified copy $1 more per document
Plat map copies$3 per page
DD Form 214 and death documents in the real estate recordsNo fee
State unemployment, sales and use tax liens; child support liensNo fee

Copies returned by mail carry a handling fee on top of the per-page charge: $1.25 for 1 to 10 pages, $2.00 for 11 to 20 pages, and $2.50 for 21 to 60 pages.

sections.h2: Getting a deed to the recorder
sections.html:
You can use the drop box, the mail or eRecording. A seller dealing with a cash buyer usually leaves this to the closing company.

  • Drop box: outside the east entrance of the main office at the Citizens Service Center, 1675 W. Garden of the Gods Road. Seal the envelope, enclose payment and add a phone number.
  • Mail: El Paso County Clerk & Recorder, Attn: Recording, P.O. Box 2007, Colorado Springs, CO 80901-2007. Put the return address on the front of the document.
  • eRecording: the county's eRecording software page covers online submission.

To get a copy of a recorded document, email copyrequests@elpasoco.com. Copy requests are answered within 48 hours, and documents recorded before 1996 are held only at the Citizens Service Center.

Most rejections come from small errors on the county's recording checklist, and a rejected deed delays the date the buyer appears in the public record.

  • Wrong fee. Recording fees are set by statute, and the county can reject a filing with the wrong amount or page count.
  • Missing documentary fee. Any exemption has to be claimed on the face of the document, or the fee is due. The consideration figure must match on the deed and the transfer declaration.
  • No grantee address. Colorado law (C.R.S. 38-35-109(2)) requires the buyer's mailing address on the deed, because it decides where future tax statements are sent.
  • Margins. C.R.S. 30-10-406(3)(a) calls for a one inch top margin and half inch left, right and bottom margins.
  • Check problems. Checks go to the El Paso County Clerk, must be signed and must not be stale dated. A bad check sends back every document stapled to it.
  • Faint notary seals. An embossed seal that is not inked will not show on the scanned image.

Recording is handled at the main office on weekdays, and the north branch takes recordings on Saturday mornings. The other branches deal with motor vehicle and driver's license business.

  • Main office, Citizens Service Center, 1675 W. Garden of the Gods Rd.: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • North, Union Town Center branch, 8830 N. Union Blvd.: Saturday, 8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. for recording.
  • Southeast, Powers branch, 5650 Industrial Place: motor vehicle only.
  • Fort Carson branch, Bldg 1525, 6351 Wetzel Ave.: motor vehicle only.

sections.h2: What the recorder does not do
sections.html:
The recorder doesn't search titles or fix ownership questions. Under C.R.S. 30-10-101(2.5c), the office is not required to search the real estate records to find a document for copying or any other purpose. Other steps belong elsewhere:

  • Releases of deed of trust go through the El Paso County Public Trustee first, at 1675 West Garden of the Gods Road, Suite 2100, before they are recorded.
  • Property tax status certificates come from the County Treasurer. A Certificate of Taxes Due costs $10.
  • If a recorded change of title doesn't show up in the assessment records after several weeks, call the County Assessor at (719) 520-6600.
  • A title company can supply an Ownership and Encumbrances report showing the current owner and any open liens.
  • Wills, probate and small estate forms are handled by the Fourth Judicial District Court at 270 S. Tejon St.

Inherited houses are common here. If a parent's name is still on the deed, updating it is a separate recording, and the clerk advises using a title company or attorney to pick the right instrument.

The clerk suggests checking the county records at least once a year for deeds or mortgages you did not sign. That matters most for vacant houses, rentals run from out of town and properties in an estate.

  • Search the recording website, www.epcrecords.com, once a year.
  • Make sure the Assessor has the right mailing address for you.
  • Call the Assessor and Treasurer if tax bills stop arriving.
  • Check a vacant property often, or ask someone you trust to do it.
  • Update the deed when a family member dies and someone else inherits.

sections.h2: El Paso County for a home seller
sections.html:
El Paso County is the most populous county in Colorado, with 730,395 residents at the 2020 census, and Colorado Springs is its seat. It covers 2,130 square miles and was one of the original 17 Colorado counties, created on November 1, 1861.

Incorporated municipalities are Colorado Springs, Fountain, Manitou Springs, Monument, Palmer Lake and Calhan. Falcon, Eastonville, Ramah and Yoder are unincorporated, so a rural or edge-of-county home can sit outside any city. Check which jurisdiction your house is in before you quote a service or fee to a buyer.

faqs.q: How much does El Paso County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: A flat $43 per document since July 1, 2025, plus a documentary fee of one cent per $100 of price on deeds over $500. Releases of deed of trust go through the Public Trustee first.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in El Paso County as an individual?
faqs.a: The county's recording page links to eRecording software for online filing. For a single deed, the drop box, the mail or your closing company are the simplest routes.

faqs.q: How long does it take to get a copy of a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Emailed copy requests are answered within 48 hours. Copies are $0.25 per page, and a certified copy costs $1 more per document.

faqs.q: Who pays the documentary fee on a house sale?
faqs.a: Colorado law puts the fee on whoever offers the deed for recording. Who covers it in a given sale depends on the purchase contract, so check the contract and ask your closing company.

faqs.q: Where is the El Paso County recording office?
faqs.a: The main office is in the Citizens Service Center at 1675 W. Garden of the Gods Road, open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Union Town Center branch at 8830 N. Union Blvd. also takes recordings on Saturdays from 8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
